sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Leeuwarden charges for street parking in tariff zones A to D and keeps permit parking for residents. By decision of 17 February 2026 the executive set the 2026 designation, in force the day after its publication on 26 February. Zones A and B charge Monday to Saturday from 08:00 to 22:00 and Sunday from 12:00 to 18:00, while zones B*, C, D and D* charge Monday to Saturday from 08:00 to 18:00 plus shopping evenings until 22:00 [0]. The 2026 tariff table, attached to a council decision of 5 November 2025, charges 3.50 euros an hour in zone A, 2.10 in zones B and B*, 1.40 in zone C and 0.90 in zones D, D* and D/WTC, with a zone D day rate of 4.60 euros [1]. A resident permit costs 286 euros a year in the city-centre zones 1 to 4 and 143 euros in zones 6 to 10, and a business permit 570 or 286 euros [2]. The parking regulation, in force in its current form from 19 June 2026, lets the executive set a permit ceiling per zone with a waiting list, and bars new permits for centre addresses where a parking-requirement exemption was granted [11]. In a council debate of October 2024 two parties moved to pilot paid parking in the blue zones, a motion text whose outcome we did not find [12]. The 2024 consultant exploration judged a zero-emission zone for delivery vans and lorries feasible within the parking ring, with 1 January 2028 considered realistic; it was a proposal, and we did not find its status [10].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The developments are about charging and bicycles. The executive said in May 2024 that grid capacity and fire-safety rules make extra charging points in the underground Oldehove and Zaailand garages undesirable, so expansion goes into the above-ground garages Hoeksterend and Klanderij, where charging cost 0.70 euros per kWh then [8]. A supplier press release of 30 September 2024 reported 76 charging points installed in the Hoeksterend garage, prepared for expansion to 352 [9]. A 2025 council proposal would fund a guarded bicycle garage under the former V&D building on Nieuwestad, for 800 to 1,300 bicycles and 1.96 million euros, with the Stichting Parkeergarages Leeuwarden as manager; we did not read the outcome [14]. A traffic decision of 30 July 2026 reserved two charging-equipped spaces at the Trefplak car park in Middelsee for electric car-sharing vehicles as a pilot [13].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The garages are run through a foundation, the Stichting Parkeergarages Leeuwarden [14]. The 2015 parking plan counted just over 5,200 spaces in the centre, nearly 1,800 paid street spaces, nearly 500 permit spaces and over 2,500 in five garages, and judged capacity on average more than sufficient, with local shortages for short shop visits at Eewal and Tweebaksmarkt; the counts date from about 2014 [5]. It made the garages the primary parking locations for visitors and set the principle that the user pays [6]. The last garage tariffs we found, decided in November 2022 for 2023 to 2025, were 1.65 euros an hour excluding VAT at Zaailand and Oldehoofsterkerkhof, with a day maximum of 8.26 euros, and 1.40 euros an hour at Klanderij, De Revius and Hoeksterend [3]; in 2017 the hourly rate at Zaailand was higher, at 2.07 euros, and the day maximum lower [4]. We did not find a decision for 2026.

Our data cover the P+R Wijnhornsterstraat, with 253 spaces, for about 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 22% on weekdays and 17% at weekends, with a peak of 56% around midday on a Tuesday. The garages in the centre are not in our data.
